source.title: When Do Concepts Become Functionally Sufficient During Language-Model Training?
source.authors: Raphael Bernas; Paul Chevalier; Fanny Jourdan; Céline Hudelot

record.tranche_reason: The study measures target-conditional functional sufficiency of sparse masks over activation decompositions, but does not test superposition geometry, capacity-driven polysemanticity, SAE feature recovery, canonical feature units, or feature dimensionality as specified by the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports results on sparse masks of SVD, ICA, NMF, and SemiNMF decompositions, including held-out predictive-distribution preservation. These bear on functional sufficiency of selected coordinates, but do not measure whether sparse features overlap as nearly orthogonal directions or test any listed version. The aggregate operating-point results are recorded as related findings with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study fits SVD, ICA, NMF and SemiNMF decompositions of MLP outputs in seven pretrained LMs. It then measures how well sparse soft masks over those coordinates preserve reconstruction, fixed-head decodability, downstream predictions and checkpoint transfer. It never measures features overlapping as nearly orthogonal directions, polysemantic neurons, SAE feature recovery, the canonicity of dictionary features, or feature dimensionality. SAEs (Bricken et al., Huben et al.) appear only as cited related methods, and superposition is not discussed. So cites_only rather than discusses.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that checkpoint-wise interventions yield target-conditional operating points, with compact output-preserving masks enriched for supervised sensitivity and structured temporal, depth and decomposition profiles. They caution that sufficiency is not unique interpretability or persistent concept identity.
record.recipe_differences: The study does not reproduce the original toy-model superposition method. It fits activation decompositions and evaluates sparse-mask preservation across checkpoints in pretrained language models.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes vary with preservation objective, decomposition, model, checkpoint, and layer. The authors also state that sufficiency depends on the chosen decomposition, sparsity operating point, and intervention operator.

fits_no_version.finding: At the shared fixed-penalty operating point, downstream-selected masks keep 6.6% soft occupancy versus 73.0% for reconstruction masks (seven-model median). Downstream masks keep relative KL at 0.020 despite reconstruction NMSE of 0.959 versus 0.215.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Much activation variance in decomposed MLP outputs lies in directions weakly used downstream; a small subset of decomposition coordinates suffices to preserve predictions.

fits_no_version.finding: Source-to-final learned-alignment transfer KL falls toward the endpoint for SVD and ICA in all seven models, but not for NMF in five models or SemiNMF in six.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-checkpoint reconstructability of decomposition coordinates depends on the decomposition family and does not imply persistent feature identities.

record.problems: One run per model; checkpoint, layer, method, and objective measurements are correlated repeated measurements. The reported comparisons use one fixed sparsity penalty rather than a matched-budget or matched-fidelity frontier. The authors state that concept identities were not retained, and that learned transfer can reflect alignment flexibility as well as continuity.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity sweep, feature-overlap or geometry measurements.
No neuron-level polysemanticity or feature-importance/capacity allocation analysis.
No analysis of the causes of polysemantic neurons.
No SAE is trained. The decompositions are dense or non-negative factorizations, and no measure of features spread across neurons is reported.
No SAE features are tested for completeness, stability or canonicity. Concept identities were not retained across checkpoints.
No test of 1-D versus multi-dimensional features. Soft occupancy is explicitly not intrinsic dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'discusses' is changed to 'cites_only' because the paper never engages with superposition or any listed version; it only cites SAE work as related concept extraction. All rows correctly carry versions ['none'] and cannot_determine. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test sparse-feature overlap, near-orthogonality, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometry in toy networks.
Does not test whether capacity competition causes polysemantic neurons or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity evidences superposition.
Does not measure features spread across neurons or whether sparse features are recovered by an SAE; its decompositions are SVD, ICA, NMF, and SemiNMF.

Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units. The paper notes that decomposition coordinates do not guarantee human interpretability and that redundant or distributed coordinates can preserve behavior.
Does not test whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional structures.

rows.operation_detail: Fit sparse soft masks for activation reconstruction and evaluate held-out interventions.
rows.baseline: Original model predictions for relative KL; not stated for soft occupancy or NMSE.
rows.note: Reports the reconstruction-mask operating point, not feature overlap or superposition geometry.

rows.subject: seven-model aggregate (median of seven within-model medians)
rows.operation_detail: Fit sparse soft masks to preserve the model's downstream predictive distribution and evaluate held-out interventions.
rows.measure: soft occupancy; relative KL; accuracy damage; NMSE
rows.baseline: Original model predictions for relative KL; original target-token top-1 accuracy for accuracy damage; reconstruction-selection NMSE comparison.
rows.value: 6.6% soft occupancy; relative KL 0.020; 0.80 percentage-point accuracy damage; NMSE 0.959 (versus 0.215 for reconstruction selection).
rows.note: Shows compact masks can preserve output distributions at this fixed penalty, but does not establish superposition or that these coordinates are model-intrinsic feature units.

rows.subject: seven-model aggregate (median of seven within-model medians)
rows.operation_detail: Fit source-checkpoint masks with learned alignment and evaluate source-to-final transfer.
rows.baseline: Original final-checkpoint predictions for relative KL; not stated for soft occupancy or NMSE.
rows.note: Transfer uses learned alignment and is reported separately from same-checkpoint objectives; it does not track identity-matched features.
